comments.author: cletus
comments.story_title: Star Citizen will limit its roadmap, as players are getting upset over delays
comments.why_zh: No Man's Sky 的糟糕首发与恢复
comments.text_zh: 看 Star Citizen 对我来说已经成了一种爱好，就像看一场慢得令人痛苦的火车事故。它出现的时间，差不多正是深受喜爱的系列 Elite 以 Elite Dangerous 的形式复兴之时。ED 没有 SC 那样的预算，但它坚持相当狭窄的开发目标，并且多年前就已经发售了。此后它逐步增加了更新、补丁和扩展内容。No Man's Sky 大致也是同一路数，首发非常糟糕（我强烈推荐这个视频 [1]），但值得称赞的是，Hello Games 一直坚持打磨 NMS，不断增加内容和更新，直到现在它已经是一款令人愉快的体验，并且拥有忠实的粉丝群体。但 SC 呢？我的天。它就像是 NFT 骗局的鼻祖。不断通过出售限量发售的飞船来筹集更多资金（为了一款基本上仍不存在的游戏）。我偶尔会看到某个正在开发的新系统的演示（比如监狱系统），我总是想：“他们连核心游戏都还没有，到底为什么要谈这个？”这是一个活生生的教训：太多钱也可能是坏事。钱多到令人难堪，太容易导致无可救药的功能蔓延，最后什么也交付不出来。老实说，我很惊讶还有这么多人对 SC 喝 Kool-Aid。我真的想知道那些钱都去哪了（以及实际上有多少已经没了）。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: Watching Star Citizen has been a hobby for me like watching a train wreck is painfully slow motion. It came about at the same time as the revival of a beloved franchise Elite in the form of Elite Dangerous. ED didn't have the budget SC does but it stuck to quite narrow development goals and shipped years ago. It's progressively added updates, patches and expansions since. No Man's Sky is vaguely in the same vein and had a terrible launch (I highly recommend this video [1]) but, to their credit, Hello Games has plugged away at NMS adding more content and updates to the point where it's an enjoyable experience now and has a loyal fan base. But SC? By God. It's like a progenitor for NFT scams. Constantly raising even more money by selling limited run ships (for a game that still basically doesn't exist). I'd occasionally see a presentation on some new system under development (eg the prison system) and I always thought "why on Earth are they talking about this before they even have a core game?" It's an object lesson that too much money can be a bad thing. It's so easy for an embarrassment of riches to lead to hopeless feature creep and not really delivering anything. I'm honestly surprised so many still drink the Kool-Aid on SC. I really wonder where all the money has gone (and how much is actually gone). [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: jmyeet
comments.story_title: Bay 12 Games has made $7M from the Steam release of Dwarf Fortress
comments.why_zh: No Man's Sky 发售失败与多年更新的故事
comments.quote_zh: 我强烈推荐 Internet Historian 关于这件事的视频 [1]。
comments.text_zh: 我真为他们高兴。他们多年来在捐款方面确实很艰难。看到他们终于赚到钱，挺好的。至于那些评论销量下滑的人，这对 AAA 大作来说确实是个问题：半成品卖给公众，然后就被抛弃了，因为直接转去做下一个项目更省事。但我想用 No Man's Sky 的故事来反驳这一点。我强烈推荐 Internet Historian 关于这件事的视频 [1]。简而言之，由于各种原因，这款游戏在发售时承诺过多、交付不足，但 Sean 和 HelloGames 如今已经花了好几年时间，持续用免费且内容扎实的更新来开发这款游戏。我只能想象这仍然在推动销量增长，否则这种模式无法持续。但这确实修复了 HG 和 NMS 的声誉。NMS 现在有了真正的忠实拥趸。当然，还有 Minecraft，它的长尾销量简直令人难以置信。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: I'm super happy for these guys. They really have struggled with donations for many years. It's nice to see them get the bag. For those commenting on the sales drop off, it is a problem for AAA titles that a half-finished product gets sold to the public and then abandoned because it's easier to just move onto the next thing. But I want to counter that with the story of No Man's Sky. I highly recommend the Internet Historian video on it [1]. The short version is for various reasons the game over-promised and under-delieved on launch but Sean and HelloGames have now spent years continuing to develop the game with free and significant updates. I can only imagine this still drives sales growth or it wouldn't be sustainable. But it's really repaired HG's and NMS's reputation. NMS has a real cult following now. And then of course there's Minecraft whose long tail of sales is truly mind-blowing. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: cletus
comments.why_zh: No Man's Sky 发售时过度承诺后的救赎
comments.quote_zh: 有一个很棒的 Internet Historian 视频 [1]，讲的是 NMS 在发售时过度承诺之后如何实现救赎。
comments.text_zh: Star Citizen 是一个警示故事，说明钱太多也可能是一种诅咒。Star Citizen 和 Elite Dangerous 差不多同时出现，但 Elite 多年来一直是一款完整的游戏。Elite 做对的地方在于，他们先发布了一款完整的游戏，然后再不断添加内容。我看过一些关于 Star Citizen 的视频，讲他们正在加入的新系统，比如把玩家关进监狱以及越狱之类的，我所能想到的就是：这听起来很酷，但你连核心游戏都还没有，为什么要在这上面花精力？Star Citizen 的开发看起来完全没有重点，还时不时靠卖飞船来填充金库。如果他们当初先确定核心特性、做出一款完整的游戏，然后每隔 6 到 12 个月发布内容更新，那会好多少？如果有人只想探索，而不想要 Elite Dangerous 那种粗粝感和过度写实，可以看看 No Man's Sky。顺便说一句，有一个很棒的 Internet Historian 视频 [1]，讲的是 NMS 在发售时过度承诺之后如何实现救赎。另外，我看到另一款游戏似乎也掉进了同样的陷阱：还没有核心玩法就过于野心勃勃，遗憾的是，那就是 Ashes of Creation。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: Star Citizen is a cautionary tale about how too much money can be a curse. Star Citizen and Elite Dangerous came around at roughly the same time but Elite has been a complete game for years. Elite did things right in the sense that they released a complete game and added to it. I've seen videos on Star Citizen talking about new systems they're adding like being put in prison and escaping and all I can think of is that this sounds cool but why are you spending any effort on this before you have a core game? star Citizen development just seems to be completely unfocused with periodic sales of ships to top up the coffers. How much better could it have been had they decided on core features that were a complete game and then just added content releases every 6-12 months? For anyone who just wants to explore without the grittiness and over-realism of Elite Dangerous, check out No Man's Sky. Side note, there's a great Internet Historian video [1] on the redemption of NMS after over-promising on release. Also, I see another game that seems to be falling into the trap of being too ambitious before having core gameplay and that's Ashes of Creation, sadly. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: snowgrove
comments.story_title: Worms or bust: The story of Britain’s most tenacious indie games company (2016)
comments.why_zh: Hello Games 在 No Man's Sky 发售后的历程
comments.quote_zh: 整个故事令人难以置信，值得你花时间看看
comments.text_zh: 我很喜欢 Worms，但如果要评选“英国最顽强的独立游戏公司”的亚军，那肯定非 Hello Games 莫属。他们在 2016 年推出 No Man's Sky，结果招来一片失望和玩家愤怒，但他们在发售之后仍坚持开发了好几年（承受着极大压力，收入也少得可怜），直到满足并超越了玩家最初的期待。心怀感激的玩家最终凑钱，在他们办公室附近的一条路上立了一块“Thank you Hello Games”的广告牌。整个故事令人难以置信，值得你花时间看看：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I love Worms, but if there’s a runner-up for “Britain’s most tenacious indie games company” then surely it is Hello Games. They launched No Man’s Sky in 2016 to universal disappointment and fan outrage, but kept working on it post-launch (under extreme stress and with little income to speak of) for years until they met & exceeded fan’s original expectations. Gratified fans eventually paid to put up a “Thank you Hello Games” billboard on a road near their office. The whole story is incredible and worth your time: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ziddoap
comments.story_title: No Man's Sky's update introduces billions of new stars, planets, and more
comments.why_zh: 很好地回顾了一次糟糕首发如何走向成功
comments.quote_zh: 《The Engoodening of No Man's Sky》很好地回顾了这段故事。
comments.text_zh: No Man's Sky 是把糟糕首发扭转为成功的典型代表。在现在这个版本里，你真能感受到 Hello Games 员工的热情。这让我想起一句我马上就要说走样的话，大意是：“人们不会记住问题本身，而是会记住你如何处理问题。”如果你还没看过，《The Engoodening of No Man's Sky》很好地回顾了这段故事。它现在已经5年了，而这场“engoodening”还没有停止。[VIDEO]
comments.text: No Man's Sky is the poster child for turning a shitty launch into a success. You can really feel the passion of the staff at Hello Games in the current version of the game. It reminds me of the quote, which I'm about to butcher, that is along the lines of "People don't remember the problem, they remember how you dealt with the problem". If you haven't seen it, "The Engoodening of No Man's Sky" is a good review of the story. It's 5 years old now, and the engoodening hasn't stopped. [VIDEO]
